scenes.say: Ever seen Git stop you with a conflict? What should you actually do next?

scenes.label: Reality
scenes.sub: Interviewers want proof you can handle real-world code clashes.
scenes.say: Interviewers want proof you can handle real-world code clashes. This is a must-have skill.

scenes.title: Git marks conflicts
scenes.say: When changes overlap, Git marks the files with a conflict. You'll see a message like this in your terminal.
Open the file. You'll spot clear markers showing both versions. Edit the code to keep what you want.
Here's the process: open the files, find the markers, edit to resolve, stage your changes, and commit. That's it.

scenes.question: What's a common mistake with conflicts?
scenes.right: You must remove all conflict markers before committing, or your code won't work.
scenes.say: Don't just commit with those markers still in the file. You have to remove them all before finishing up.
